primitives.name: Measurable Section Preservation
primitives.verbatim_quote: It follows that every section of a measurable set [or a measurable function] is a measurable set [or a measurable function].
primitives.assumptions: Let (X, S) be a measurable space and let A ⊆ X. Then for any fixed x ∈ X, the section A_x = {y : (x,y) ∈ A} is measurable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sections fail to preserve measurability due to non-Borel sets or improper σ-algebra choices.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's conditional probability framework, where sections correspond to posterior distributions over subsets of joint spaces.
layer2.telemetry: Verification via Borel set containment under projection maps.

primitives.name: Cartesian Product Measure Uniqueness
primitives.verbatim_quote: Proceeding by mathematical induction, it is now trivial to define the Cartesian product of σ-finite measure spaces (Xi,Si,μi), i = 1, ··., n; there is one and only one measure μ (denoted by μ1 ×·.·× μn) on S1 ×···× Sn such that for every measurable rectangle A1..· An.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'μ': 'measure on product space', 'μ_i': 'σ-finite measure on space X_i'}
primitives.assumptions: Each (X_i, S_i, μ_i) is a σ-finite measure space; the product measure is uniquely defined on the product σ-ring.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when individual measures are not σ-finite or when the product σ-ring is not well-defined.

layer2.mapping: Derived kernel in GSE for constructing joint probability distributions from independent marginals.
layer2.telemetry: Validation via consistency of product integrals against component integrals.

primitives.name: Fubini Extension
primitives.verbatim_quote: The extension of Fubini's theorem is also immediate, so that the integral of any integrable function in a product space may be evaluated by forming the iterated integral in any order.
primitives.latex: \int_{X_1 \times \cdots \times X_n} f d\mu = \int_{X_1} \left( \cdots \int_{X_n} f(x_1,\ldots,x_n) dx_n \right) dx_1
primitives.assumptions: Function f is integrable with respect to the product measure μ; Fubini’s theorem applies to σ-finite spaces.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When integrability fails or when the order of integration cannot be interchanged due to discontinuity or unboundedness.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI’s iterative expectation computation in high-dimensional belief propagation.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation of iterated integral results using different integration orders.

Measurable sections ensure that projections maintain the integrity of measurable sets, allowing for consistent probabilistic interpretation. Fubini’s extension enables flexible evaluation of integrals through iterated operations, which is essential for computational tractability in complex systems. These primitives form a coherent basis for both theoretical analysis and practical implementation in GSI and GSE frameworks.
